correctness.rationale: Only the (2,1,1) multiplicity pattern changes the accuracy under deletion averaging: for a doubled true label the gain is 1/3; for a doubled false label it is −1/6. The (2,2) case averages its fair tie correctly, and the two-label identity follows by omitting (2,1,1). The four stated probability vectors generate the modal simplex slice by the supplied nonnegative convex coefficients. Independence gives separate affineness. I independently computed the 35 multiset types by multiplying integer generating polynomials for their uniform supports and extracting the three (2,1,1) coefficients; every table value matches and 0012 is the only maximizing vertex type. In it A4=1, and the outcome which gives the gain 1/3 occurs with probability 1/4, giving A3=11/12. The general N argument is exact because each triple has N−3 four-element extensions and each extension deletes to that triple with probability 1/4.
residual_risks: The cap is sharp across the stated class via N=4, not asserted sharp for each separately fixed N>4. Dependence, other choice or committee sizes, and nonuniform tie-breaking are outside scope.

value.rationale: This adjacent odd-to-even comparison distinguishes ternary accuracy from an identically flat binary comparison. The deterministic gain has both signs, so monotonicity under independent weak modal competence is a genuine restriction, especially with different error directions. The exact 1/12 envelope and an explicit attaining panel give a finite, interpretable benchmark for multiclass judging from randomly staffed panels.
residual_risks: No broader committee-size trend, strategic outcome, or asymptotic rate follows.
